public_rationale: Contemporaneous evaluations document recurring factual errors across multiple model families and tasks. That supports the ordinary reading that users still needed to check LLM answers. The evidence also shows improvements; Marcus’s statement does not require accuracy to have remained unchanged.
limitations: The finding concerns general factual dependability, not every task or application.
The evidence uses task-specific evaluations rather than a representative sample of all user requests.
Evaluation months identify when the findings were reported; exact test-run dates are not supplied in the cited passages.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs remained unreliable as of April 2024, a year after Choi's TED talk.

statement.excerpt: Yejin Choi worried that LLMs were not reliable. They still aren’t.
statement.document_title: TED, AI, and the test of time

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that general-purpose LLMs continued to make recurring factual or reasoning errors that prevented users from depending on their answers without checking.
This does not mean that every answer was wrong, that no application was reliable, or that models had stopped improving.
Use the most recent completed quarter before publication, January through March 2024, for contemporaneous evaluations. Marcus supplied no reporting period or numerical reliability threshold.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous evaluations across multiple prominent models document recurring factual or reasoning errors in substantive tasks.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad contemporaneous evaluations establish dependable factual and reasoning performance across the claimed scope, with failures confined to exceptional cases.

evidence.explanation: The March evaluation covers thirteen models from the Gemini, GPT, Claude and PaLM-2 families and documents continuing factuality limitations. It also finds better performance among larger models, so it supports continued unreliability without supporting stagnation.

Human annotations identify recurring factual errors in topic-focused dialogue summaries. This supplies evidence from another substantive task, although it does not establish an error rate for all uses.
